claims.sentence: The MHRA authorised Inqlexzo, a gemcitabine system placed in the bladder, for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
claims.evidence: Page: MHRA authorised an intravesical delivery system containing gemcitabine (Inqlexzo) for certain bladder cancers incl. BCG-unresponsive HR-NMIBC.

claims.sentence: The MHRA authorised the gemcitabine delivery system Inqlexzo for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
It is for adults who cannot have, or choose not to have, surgery to remove the bladder.
claims.evidence: Page: for adults ineligible for, or who chose not to undergo, radical cystectomy.

claims.sentence: A healthcare professional places the system in the bladder using a catheter, and it releases gemcitabine locally.
claims.evidence: Page: healthcare professional places it via catheter; sustained local release of gemcitabine over about three weeks.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says it will keep monitoring the safety and effectiveness of the system.
claims.evidence: Page: MHRA will keep safety and effectiveness under review.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says it has authorised an intravesical gemcitabine delivery system, Inqlexzo, for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
The authorisation covers adults who are ineligible for, or have chosen not to have, radical cystectomy, which is surgery to remove the bladder.
claims.evidence: Page: ineligible for or chosen not to undergo radical cystectomy (bladder removal surgery).

claims.sentence: A healthcare professional places the device in the bladder using a catheter, and it releases the chemotherapy medicine gemcitabine inside the bladder.
claims.evidence: Page says the system releases gemcitabine; that gemcitabine is a chemotherapy medicine is textbook, not stated in the retrieved text.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says the authorisation is supported by results from a clinical study in adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk disease and carcinoma in situ.
claims.evidence: Page: supported by results from a clinical study in adults with BCG-unresponsive HR-NMIBC with carcinoma in situ.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says it will keep monitoring the safety and effectiveness of the system.
The site's bladder cancer page explains the condition.
claims.evidence: Not a statement from the source page; an internal-link sentence the retrieved text does not contain.

dateEvidence: Not readable. Search 3 returned an MHRA notes entry giving the marketing authorisation grant date as 24 June 2026 (Janssen-Cilag Ltd, International Recognition Procedure Route B). Two searches described the news page only as 'about 124 days old' (about 2 July 2026 counted back from 3 Nov). No result printed '1 July 2026'. The brief's 1 July is therefore unconfirmed.
notes: Publication date 1 July NOT confirmed (age estimate ~2 July; grant date 24 June). No complete-response percentage was stated in any retrieved GOV.UK text (the 82% figure from the first pass is unsupported; the brief correctly omits it). Recommend either verifying the date on the page before publishing or setting published/source.published to the verified date; text itself is safe.
